chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā together, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about water from which pigeons drink, and he said: “Everything whose flesh is eaten, wudu (ablution) may be performed from its leftover water, and it may be drunk.”

His statement, “Everything whose flesh is eaten, wudu (ablution) may be performed with its leftover water and it may be drunk,” indicates that everything whose flesh is not eaten, wudu (ablution) with it and drinking from it are not permitted. For when the permissibility of its leftover water is made conditional upon its flesh being eaten, that indicates that whatever is other than it is contrary to that; and this proceeds in that manner.

key_terms.الشُّرْبُ: drinking or consumption of the water
key_terms.الْحَمَامُ: pigeons or doves that drink from the water
key_terms.سُؤْرِهِ: the leftover water remaining after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water under discussion for ritual and ordinary use
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: whose meat is lawful to eat

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with water left over by animals that drink from it?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the leftover water of animals whose meat is halal may be used for wudu (ablution) and may also be drunk. The accompanying legal analysis infers from this that the leftover water of animals whose meat is not eaten is not permitted for wudu (ablution) or drinking. The text is a juristic discussion concerning ritual purity and the rulings of animal leftovers.
